title: Tanzanian Chicken Skewers
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Mishkaki ya Kuku — chicken thigh cubes marinated in garlic, ginger, lime, and Tanzanian spices, grilled over charcoal until golden and juicy. The lighter, popular alternative to beef mishkaki — equally beloved and found at every street food jiko.
longDesc: Chicken mishkaki are the street food of Tanzania's health-conscious — lighter than beef but equally fragrant and satisfying. Chicken thigh is always used — it stays juicy over charcoal where breast would dry out.
steps: Mix marinade. Toss chicken in marinade. Refrigerate 2 hours.
Grill over medium-high coals 3—4 minutes per side.
Serve with chapati and pili pili.
chefTips: Chicken thighs only — breast dries out.
Test doneness — no pink in the centre.
cookingScience: Chicken thigh myoglobin content gives the meat more moisture retention at high temperatures compared to breast — the fat marbling within the muscle fibres keeps the thigh juicy even when the surface is charred.
culturalNote: Chicken mishkaki has become the preferred street food of Tanzania's growing middle class — the lighter option at the jiko that still delivers all the satisfaction of the charcoal-grilled experience.
